name: Lazarus RipperDoc Street Clinic Full Rig
description:
Street ripperdoc's complete working set: a long-sleeved antimicrobial wrap-coat in deep teal with brown burn-stains that no amount of washing removes, over a sealed nitrile underlayer. Surgical cap is recycled poly-weave, ear loops reinforced with wire to accommodate horn or fin geneware. Face shield is scratched but intact. Apron front has tiered tool loops — scalpels, probe leads, cable management clips.

Feet: sealed boot-covers over heavy rubber-soled work boots, non-slip tread. Gloves are double-layered — inner BCI-conductive, outer disposable nitrile. The whole rig smells faintly of isopropyl and ozone. Nothing matches. Everything functions.
functionality: Antimicrobial outer layer, BCI-conductive inner gloves for interface during surgery, sealed nitrile underlayer for biohazard protection, tool-loop apron, non-slip boot covers, gene-compatible surgical cap with reinforced loops.
what_it_says: This person fixes what the licensed clinics won't touch, for people who can't afford to ask questions.
story_hooks: The burn stains on the coat are not from surgery — the ripperdoc won't say what caused them.
The BCI-conductive gloves are a licensed Lazarus model, far too expensive for a Shelf clinic — someone is supplying this doc.
A patient recognizes the tool-loop apron's stitching pattern as belonging to a Tier-4 surgical suite that went dark six months ago.
